solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Madden left-leaning party before the last pamphlet

indicators.note: in an across clue, leaning to the left means the letters run right to left, so this word is read backwards
the party word stops just short of its final letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: A political tract from a left-wing party, published before the final one, drives someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left-leaning' looks political but is the reversal signal for an across entry; 'before the last' trims the party word. Solvers on the blog needed a commenter's help with this one.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden can mean to drive to distraction, an old sense of distract being to make frantic.

clue.text: Poem dismissing old rebel of the 60s perhaps

indicators.note: the poem sends away one of its letters, which is removed

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450

explanation.surface: A poem about an old rebel from the Sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebel of the 60s' suggests a hippy; the rebel is Jack Cade, and 'the 60s perhaps' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sixties are an example of a decade, a ten-year span.

clue.text: Unhappy implicating cool British sailor of fiction

indicators.note: to implicate is to involve, so the unhappy word folds the others inside it

parts.note: sad means unhappy
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: An unhappy man drags a cool British seaman from a novel into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad the Sailor is the hero of voyages in the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Foolish talk powerless to disconcert

indicators.note: P is the physics symbol for power, and without power it is removed

parts.note: prattle is silly, childish chatter

explanation.surface: Silly chatter lacks the power to unsettle anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve or fluster them.

clue.text: Study by Galen vigorously maintaining it's present at birth

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the scrambled name holds the small word
the name is shaken up vigorously into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A study by the Greek physician Galen strongly argues that a condition exists from birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Galen was a Greek physician, which makes the medical surface convincing; his name is only anagram fodder, with 'vigorously' the signal and 'maintaining' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A congenital condition is one a person is born with.

clue.text: Seat of the Oracle displayed in Philadelphia

indicators.note: the answer is on show inside the letters of the city name that follows

explanation.surface: A famous Greek shrine has a namesake on view in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi in ancient Greece housed the oracle of Apollo, consulted through its priestess.

clue.text: Withdraw clergyman right away after first showings of extremist violent attacks

indicators.note: the shortened clergyman comes after the initials in the answer
the first letter on show of each of the next three words
the letter for right is sent away from the clergyman

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman

explanation.surface: A clergyman gets away fast after the first signs of extremist violence.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate a place is to withdraw people from it, or to leave it.

clue.text: Secretly planning, last of all, to share pocket money with a hint of gratitude

indicators.note: the letter comes to share the pocket's space, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pot is a pocket on a snooker or billiards table, and also to pocket a ball is to pot it

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: tin is slang for money

indicators.note: just a trace of the word, its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone schemes to split pocket money and add a touch of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket money' reads as one phrase but splits into two separate synonyms, with 'to share' putting a letter inside the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Plotting means scheming or conspiring in secret.

clue.text: Henry oddly neglected to go with popular type of grass

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a form is a kind or type

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of the name are passed over, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Henry ignored the instruction to choose a popular variety of lawn grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of grass' looks like lawn seed; grass is British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is someone who informs to the police.

clue.text: Incessant pious platitudes about working on street

indicators.note: the platitudes go round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone keeps spouting sanctimonious clichés while working on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant never stops, the same as incessant, a near synonym.

clue.text: Managed to get out of continuity when produced quickly

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, so ran means managed
a show or event that is off has been taken out of its continuing run, discontinued

explanation.surface: Someone managed to escape the tedium of continuity work once filming was rushed through.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off copies is to print or produce them fast, an idiom from duplicating machines.

clue.text: That's stopping wobbly ladder becoming more likely to cause death

indicators.note: the short piece plugs a gap in the scrambled ladder, as a stopper fills a hole
a wobbly thing is unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Steadying a wobbly ladder stops it becoming more dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stopping' reads as halting the ladder, but it means plugging: the abbreviation goes inside the anagram that 'wobbly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadlier is the comparative of deadly, meaning more lethal or more fatal.

clue.text: More appealing to skirt the west end of Thasos by boat

indicators.note: to skirt is to go round the edge, so the comparative wraps around the single letter

parts.note: cuter means more charming or appealing

indicators.note: in an across entry the west end of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: It is more charming to sail around the western tip of the Greek island of Thasos.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutter is a small, fast sailing vessel or a ship's boat.

clue.text: Be 50/50 over Welsh number becoming a standard setter

indicators.note: in a down entry the first pieces sit over, above, the rest

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties are LL
ether numbs, so it is a 'number', an old anaesthetic

explanation.surface: Splitting things evenly over a Welsh figure makes one a benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' is something that numbs: ETHER, an early anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellwether is the leading sheep of a flock, so figuratively a trendsetter or indicator others follow.

clue.text: Dabbler in art of French island race taken in by Italian poet

indicators.note: the poet takes the other pieces into himself, enclosing them

parts.note: Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy
île is French for island
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: An amateur dabbling in art of a French island race gets fooled by an Italian poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is an amateur who takes up the arts superficially, a dabbler.

clue.text: Embarrasses female after trick ends

indicators.note: the female letter comes after the trick in the answer

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
uses are ends or purposes

explanation.surface: Embarrassment comes to a woman once a trick finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To confuse someone can mean to abash or fluster them, close to embarrassing them.

clue.text: Loyal supporter of Soviet leader not concerned with western guile

indicators.note: the soviet leader is taken without the small word for concerned with

parts.note: Joseph Stalin led the Soviet Union
in means involved or concerned with, as in 'in on the plan'
art can mean cunning or craft, guile

explanation.surface: A loyal follower of Stalin is not bothered by Western cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart is a dependable, committed supporter of a cause or party.

clue.text: Representative of English stage involved in romantic engagement

indicators.note: the pieces are wrapped up inside the date

parts.note: a date is a romantic appointment
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: An English delegate's stage of the trip is tangled up in a love affair.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegate is a person sent to represent others at a meeting.

clue.text: Offered for discussion in letter received by surprised noble

indicators.note: the letter is taken in by the scrambled noble, sitting inside it
being surprised throws one off balance, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: theta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A letter received by an astonished aristocrat is up for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' suggests correspondence, but it is a Greek alphabet letter; 'surprised' signals the anagram and 'received by' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal on the table has been put forward for debate, an idiom from the meeting room.

clue.text: Crucial index oddly dismissed by Scotland's top economist

parts.note: key means crucial or essential

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are sent off, keeping the even ones
in a down entry the top of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A crucial index is dropped by Scotland's leading economist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist behind Keynesian theory.

clue.text: More acceptable in prison

explanation.surface: Things are more tolerable inside jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooler works as a comparative of cool, and as slang for jail.

clue.text: Drew regularly on Native American law

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second
every other letter of the name, taken at regular intervals

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: Drew habitually relies on a Native American legal code.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official order having the force of law.

clue.text: Speak hesitantly of bird mostly seen on river

indicators.note: in an across entry the bird piece sits on, next to, the river after it

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, England

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter cut off

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone stammers when talking of a bird spotted perched on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To falter in speech is to stammer or speak with hesitation.

clue.text: Girl coming from working people around the Newcastle area

indicators.note: the scrambled people go around the area letters, holding them inside
letters set to work are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: Newcastle upon Tyne is in North East England, NE

explanation.surface: A girl from a working-class family in the Newcastle area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working people' reads as the working class, but 'working' is the anagram signal; 'around' puts the region's abbreviation inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Penelope is a girl's name, from the faithful wife of Odysseus.

clue.text: Hospital embracing amateur medicine man

indicators.note: the hospital wraps its arms round the amateur, enclosing him

parts.note: a san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
a ham is an amateur, especially a radio enthusiast or a poor actor

explanation.surface: A hospital welcomes an amateur healer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer and spiritual figure, called a medicine man.

clue.text: Old shopkeeper and city worker joining the French Resistance

parts.note: C stands for city, as in the C of EC for the City of London area
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
le is French for the
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A former shopkeeper and a City worker sign up with the French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: Some solvers thought C for city loose; it occurs in postcodes such as EC (East Central).
explanation.definitionFit: A chandler once made and sold candles, and later sold ship's supplies, a trade now mostly historical.

clue.text: A dog for me

definitions.meaning: a ... is a gun dog breed, such as the Irish ...
the ... of a crossword refers to himself as 'me' in clues

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a dog for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Setter names both a hunting breed and the compiler of the puzzle, who here is the speaker.

clue.text: Retain perverse cook

indicators.note: to cook books is to falsify them, so the letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: Keep hold of a contrary chef.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep or maintain it, the same as retain.
